definitions.gloss: to trample down, to knock down by stepping on
definitions.explanation: To knock something or someone down by stepping on or trampling.

definitions.gloss: to default on, to skip out on (payment)
definitions.explanation: To fail to pay a debt or bill, especially with no intention of paying. Often implies running away from the obligation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{花壇|かだん}→花壇：11075_kadan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}してしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally trampled down the flowers in the flower bed.

examples.japanese: ⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{稲|いね}→稲：01820_ine⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}された⟦ように→ように：10081_youni⟧⟦なっている→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The rice plants look like they've been trampled down by the wind.

examples.japanese: ⟦{群衆|ぐんしゅう}→群衆：14930_gunshuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{柵|さく}→柵：13103_saku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}して⟦{会場|かいじょう}→会場：01269_kaijou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: The crowd trampled down the fences and entered the venue.

examples.japanese: ⟦{借金|しゃっきん}→借金：03203_shakkin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}して⟦{逃|に}げた→逃げる：01151_nigeru⟧。
examples.english: He skipped out on his debt and ran away.

examples.english: There are customers who skip out on their restaurant bills.

examples.japanese: ⟦{家賃|やちん}→家賃：03639_yachin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}されて⟦{困|こま}っている→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: I'm in trouble because someone defaulted on rent payments.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB: ⟦{踏|ふ}む→踏む：01197_fumu⟧ (to step on) + ⟦{倒|たお}す→倒す：01954_taosu⟧ (to knock down) = to step on and knock down

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive. Takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ to mark what is being trampled or the debt being defaulted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・⟦{借金|しゃっきん}→借金：03203_shakkin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す (to default on a debt)
・⟦{家賃|やちん}→家賃：03639_yachin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す (to skip out on rent)
・⟦{飲|の}み{代|だい}→飲み代：noentry⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す (to dine and dash)
・⟦ツケ→ツケ：noentry⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{踏|ふ}み{倒|たお}す (to skip out on a tab)

NUANCE: Sense 2 (defaulting on payment) is the more common usage in everyday conversation. It carries a strong negative connotation of dishonesty and irresponsibility.
